evidence: Receiving DO2 collapse at t=46.2h: 12.25 -> 3.69 mg/L (receiving_observations)
DO2 at/below 2.0 mg/L minimum: 1.67 (51.8h), 1.73 (52.0h), 1.96-2.4 range over 48-52h
Source batches maintained DO2 >= ~7.4 mg/L throughout 96h — receiving-specific oxygen transfer failure
Product still rising: P=0.90 g/L @36h, 2.33 g/L @48h (delayed assays)
Forward model: strong_feed_reduction gives lowest oxygen deficit 3.79 mg-h/L, min DO 1.16 mg/L, highest product mass 131.8 kg; all other actions worse (deficit 6.5-8.2)
submission.rationale: Receiving batch suffers an oxygen-transfer failure: DO2 collapsed from ~12 to ~3.3 mg/L at 46.2 h and is now fluctuating at/below the 2.0 mg/L minimum (1.67-2.3 mg/L at 48-52 h), unlike any source batch. Product is still accumulating (0.90 -> 2.33 g/L from 36 to 48 h), so oxygen demand remains high. Among bounded interventions, the source-calibrated forward model (imperfect, transfer multiplier ~0.44) ranks strong_feed_reduction best: lowest oxygen deficit (3.79 vs 6.5-8.2 mg-h/L), highest retained product mass (131.8 kg, since reduced feed lowers dilution volume), while cutting metabolic oxygen demand 40% and raising aeration 15%. Stop yields zero counted production; keep continues the violation. Recommend strong feed reduction with 15% air increase, with continued DO2 monitoring.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated, not receiving-truth; all its sensitivity members show post-decision DO2 remaining below 2.0 mg/L, so no bounded action is projected to fully clear the constraint. Strong_feed_reduction is the best bounded mitigation, not a guaranteed fix — actual receiving kinetics, oxygen demand, and transfer capacity are hidden. If DO2 remains below 2 mg/L after the change, escalation beyond the bounded menu would be warranted.

evidence: Receiving DO2 collapse at 46.2h: 12.2 -> 3.7 mg/L, then to ~1.7-2.4 mg/L through 52h
Sub-floor DO2 readings: 1.97 (50.2h), 1.96 (51.0h), 1.67 (51.8h), 1.73 (52.0h) vs minimum_do_mg_l = 2.0
Receiving P(48h)=2.33 g/L vs source-1/2/3 at 48h: 3.06/3.02/2.98 g/L (~25% deficit)
Source DO2 dips (e.g. ~24h in source-1) recover by 28h; receiving dip persists to 52h - not a normal transient
Source trajectories show DO2 floor of ~7.4-9 mg/L at comparable late times; receiving is far outside that envelope
submission.rationale: Receiving DO2 collapsed at ~46 h from ~12 mg/L to below the 2.0 mg/L oxygen floor (readings 1.67-1.96 at 50-52 h), indicating oxygen demand exceeding transfer capacity in the receiving vessel. A KEEP would leave an active constraint violation. Combined intervention (feed 0.8x, air 1.15x) attacks both sides of the oxygen balance with a bounded, reversible action: it restores DO2 margin above the floor while retaining 80% of feed and all accumulated product mass. Increase_air alone (15%) may be insufficient given the depth of the collapse; strong_feed_reduction sacrifices disproportionate production for margin we likely do not need; stop yields zero counted production. No extra assay requested because the 4 h turnaround delays action while the process sits at/below the DO floor under KEEP.
submission.uncertainty: Hidden receiving parameters (kLa, biomass, substrate) are unobservable; magnitude of demand reduction from a 20% feed cut is estimated, not measured. If demand is driven mainly by high biomass rather than feed, combined may under-deliver and strong_feed_reduction would be the fallback; if transfer capacity is nearly adequate, increase_air alone would have sufficed and combined costs some feed-driven production. The receiving assay history is limited to 4 h lags, so product benefit is only indirectly estimated from the source trajectories.
